key_insight: Adversarially removing one clinical covariate at a time can reveal whether a prostate MRI grading model is relying on useful disease signal or on shortcut information.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help build MRI grading models that generalize better by keeping informative variables like PSA and prostate volume while reducing dependence on potentially non-transferable factors such as age, BMI, or alcohol use.
method: Modeled MRI appearance and ISUP grade as observations of latent tumor pathology rather than treating MRI as a direct cause of grade.
Used an adversarial probing framework to suppress decodability of individual clinical covariates while preserving grade prediction.
Compared performance changes after suppressing each covariate to label variables as nuisance, proxy, or task-relevant.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 2,903 prostate MRI examinations with external validation on 576 patients and found that suppressing age, BMI, and alcohol use improved AUC, while suppressing PSA and prostate volume reduced AUC.
watch_item: Adversarial suppression shows association in the learned representation, but it does not by itself prove causal biology or guarantee better performance across all external clinical settings.
paper_title: Causal-Adversarial Probing of Clinical Covariates for Prostate MRI Grading
